summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: @servicetitan/design-system@14.5.7 is published as a React component library, but its package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun (pinned to v1.3.13), unpacks it, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. math_init.js is a 727KB file tagged `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a rotated string-array dispatcher and hex/codepoint-encoded identifiers; it is not referenced by the package's declared `main` (`./dist/system.js`, which only re-exports UI components/hooks) and has no relation to a UI design system. Using an alternate runtime to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled payload at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the obfuscated payload runs on `npm install` with the installer's privileges under a runtime chosen specifically to bypass Node-based supply-chain inspection, and its actual behavior is only observable inside the downloaded Bun process. The combination of a UI-library publisher scope with an install-time alternate-runtime execution path and an obfuscated 727KB payload is consistent with a compromised or impersonated release of the @servicetitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
